Levant update: The oil market has been sold heavily for two days on speculation there is more progress on a deal than announced.

A strong sign comes today with Iran and Oman agreeing on a shipping lane in the past few minutes and a joint project to clear mines.

The US seemed to front-run the announcement with Trump saying that mines are already clear.

The joint statement says (translated): His Excellency Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Al Busaidi, Minister of Foreign Affairs, paid a working visit to the Islamic Republic of Iran, during which he held constructive consultations with his Iranian counterpart, His Excellency Dr. Seyed Abbas Araghchi.

The consultations focused on the importance both countries attach to the resumption of safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, in a manner that safeguards their sovereignty and sovereign rights.

The two ministers discussed a phased framework that could provide a practical and implementable basis in light of the current situation in the Strait resulting from the recent war and its tragic consequences.

The proposed framework includes the establishment of a temporary joint maritime navigation corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as an agreement to carry out a joint project to clear mines from the Strait.

Technical negotiations between the two sides will also continue with the aim of reaching an agreement on a permanent navigation corridor and future arrangements for the management of the Strait, alongside establishing a mechanism for exchanging information, managing maritime traffic, and providing the related navigational and security services.

Scoreboard update: An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics.

Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.
